stem: A client with cancer-related fatigue says, 'I think I should stay in bed all day so I do not waste any energy.' Which response by the nurse is most appropriate?

options.A: Plan short rest periods and prioritize the activities that matter most, but balance rest with an individualized level of physical activity rather than remaining completely inactive.
options.B: Complete bed rest is the preferred fatigue-management strategy because physical activity reliably worsens cancer-related fatigue.
options.C: Ignore fatigue when planning the day and complete all usual activities at the same pace regardless of symptoms.
options.D: Avoid discussing activity with the healthcare team because fatigue-management strategies do not need to be individualized.

rationale: A is correct. NCI recommends planned rest, prioritizing the most important activities, and doing activities when energy is highest. NCI also supports individualized physical activity and exercise because activity can reduce cancer-related fatigue and help maintain function; complete inactivity is not the general goal. B is incorrect because routine complete bed rest can promote deconditioning and is not NCI's recommended fatigue strategy. C is incorrect because pacing and prioritization are appropriate when fatigue interferes with function. D is incorrect because activity should be individualized to the client's condition, treatment, safety, and functional ability.
educational_objective: Teach balanced energy conservation for cancer-related fatigue by combining prioritization and short planned rest with individualized safe activity rather than complete inactivity or indiscriminate overexertion.
source_organization: National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health
source_document_title: Fatigue and Cancer; Fatigue (PDQ®) — Health Professional Version; Physical Activity and Cancer Fact Sheet
source_locator: Fatigue and Cancer — management bullets under 'Rest and sleep' and 'Exercise and physical activity'; Fatigue PDQ — 'Patient Education' and exercise evidence sections, including scheduling important activities during times of least fatigue and encouraging planned exercise within individual limitations; Physical Activity and Cancer Fact Sheet — section 'Is physical activity beneficial for cancer survivors?'.
source_claim_supported: Cancer-related fatigue management includes planned rest, prioritization and scheduling of important activities, plus individualized physical activity/exercise rather than complete inactivity.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — activity/rest balance, energy conservation, symptom management, and maintenance of functional comfort.
correction_summary: Upgraded the source energy-conservation item to remove the false implication that fatigue management is mainly rest. The final item balances pacing and planned rest with individualized activity and avoids any unsupported universal exercise dose.
audit_findings: NCI directly supports prioritization, short planned rest, and scheduling activities when energy is highest.
NCI evidence also supports individualized physical activity/exercise for reducing fatigue; complete inactivity is not the recommended default.
No fixed exercise frequency, intensity, duration, or rest schedule is asserted.
Distractors represent realistic extremes—bed rest, pushing through symptoms, and non-individualized care—and only A is defensible.
Independent adversarial review found no second answer, cueing, unsupported exercise prescription, locator defect, blueprint mismatch, or unresolved conflict.
